2. Certificate of Formation (Texas LLC), Texas Secretary of State. Filed online in SOSDirect, or by mail or fax. Fee: $300. https://www.sos.state.tx.us/corp/forms/205_boc.pdf
3. Assumed Name Certificate (DBA), Texas Secretary of State. Filed when the store trades under a name other than the legal name. Fee: $25. https://www.sos.state.tx.us/corp/forms/503_boc.pdf
4. Texas Sales and Use Tax Permit Application, Texas Comptroller of Public Accounts. Apply online in eSystems before your first sale; one permit for each location. Fee: Free. https://comptroller.texas.gov/taxes/permit/
5. Certified food manager, Texas Department of State Health Services. At least one manager passes an exam from a DSHS-licensed certified food manager program. Local health departments require a certified food manager on site whenever the place is open. Fee: Varies. https://www.dshs.texas.gov/food-managers
6. Food handler certificates for staff, Texas Department of State Health Services. Every employee who works with unpackaged food, equipment or food-contact surfaces finishes an accredited food handler course within 30 days of hire. Certified food managers are exempt. Fee: Varies. https://www.dshs.texas.gov/food-handlers
7. Unemployment tax account, Texas Workforce Commission. Register online once you pay wages in Texas. Fee: Free. https://www.twc.texas.gov/services/register-tax
8. Certificate of Occupancy, City of Dallas Planning and Development. Apply on DallasNow with the land use questionnaire, plus site and floor plans if the use is changing. Needed for a new tenant or a change of use. Fee: $375. https://dallascityhall.com/departments/sustainabledevelopment/buildinginspection/Pages/certificate_occupancy.aspx
9. Building permit for tenant finish-out, City of Dallas Planning and Development. Apply on DallasNow under Commercial Permits, upload the plans and checklists, and pay online. Fee: Varies. https://dallascityhall.com/departments/sustainabledevelopment/buildinginspection/pages/fees.aspx
10. Food establishment plan review, City of Dallas Planning and Development, Health Plan Review. Submit two sets of plans, equipment sheets, finishes and the menu at 320 E. Jefferson Blvd., where the plans are reviewed and stamped. Fee: $200. https://dallascityhall.com/departments/sustainabledevelopment/buildinginspection/Pages/Health-Inspections.aspx
11. Food establishment permit, City of Dallas Code Compliance, Consumer Health. File CCS-FRM-424 with photo ID, the Texas sales tax permit and the fee, then book the health inspection. A registered food manager must be on site. Fee: $121. https://dallascityhall.com/departments/codecompliance/consumer-health/Pages/food-establishment.aspx
12. Sign permit, City of Dallas Planning and Development. A registered sign contractor applies on DallasNow once the Certificate of Occupancy is approved. Fee: $296. https://dallascityhall.com/departments/sustainabledevelopment/buildinginspection/Pages/Signs.aspx
13. Kitchen hood fire-extinguishing system permit, Dallas Fire-Rescue. Get the application from Dallas Fire-Rescue, 1551 Baylor St., Suite 400. Fee: $250. https://dallascityhall.com/departments/fire-rescue/Pages/Prevention-and-Investigation-Bureau.aspx
14. Franchise tax annual report, Texas Comptroller of Public Accounts. Filed every year by May 15, even when no tax is due. Fee: Free. https://comptroller.texas.gov/taxes/franchise/

8. Cosmetic product listing (MoCRA), U.S. Food and Drug Administration. Filed online in Cosmetics Direct by the brand (the responsible person on the label), one listing per product. Fee: Free. https://www.fda.gov/cosmetics/registration-listing-cosmetic-product-facilities-and-products
9. Product safety certificate, filed electronically at entry, U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission. The importer issues the certificate itself (there is no government form) and, under the eFiling rule, files the certificate data with CBP at entry. Fee: Free. https://www.cpsc.gov/eFiling
10. Unemployment tax account, Texas Workforce Commission. Register online once you pay wages in Texas. Fee: Free. https://www.twc.texas.gov/services/register-tax

6. Customs Bond, U.S. Customs and Border Protection. Bought from a CBP-approved surety, usually through your customs broker, who files it electronically. A continuous bond covers a year of entries. Fee: Varies. https://www.cbp.gov/sites/default/files/2024-05/cbp_form_301.pdf
7. Cosmetic product facility registration (MoCRA), U.S. Food and Drug Administration. Filed online in Cosmetics Direct by the facility that makes or processes the cosmetics. Fee: Free. https://www.fda.gov/cosmetics/registration-listing-cosmetic-product-facilities-and-products
8. Cosmetic product listing (MoCRA), U.S. Food and Drug Administration. Filed online in Cosmetics Direct by the brand (the responsible person on the label), one listing per product. Fee: Free. https://www.fda.gov/cosmetics/registration-listing-cosmetic-product-facilities-and-products
9. Product safety certificate, filed electronically at entry, U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission. The importer issues the certificate itself (there is no government form) and, under the eFiling rule, files the certificate data with CBP at entry. Fee: Free. https://www.cpsc.gov/eFiling
10. Unemployment tax account, Texas Workforce Commission. Register online once you pay wages in Texas. Fee: Free. https://www.twc.texas.gov/services/register-tax

2. Certificate of Formation (Texas LLC), Texas Secretary of State. Filed online in SOSDirect, or by mail or fax. Fee: $300. https://www.sos.state.tx.us/corp/forms/205_boc.pdf
3. Assumed Name Certificate (DBA), Texas Secretary of State. Filed when the store trades under a name other than the legal name. Fee: $25. https://www.sos.state.tx.us/corp/forms/503_boc.pdf
4. Texas Sales and Use Tax Permit Application, Texas Comptroller of Public Accounts. Apply online in eSystems before your first sale; one permit for each location. Fee: Free. https://comptroller.texas.gov/taxes/permit/
5. Create/Update Importer Identity Form, U.S. Customs and Border Protection. Sent to CBP (usually through your customs broker), or created in the ACE portal. Needed before your first entry as importer of record. Fee: Free. https://www.cbp.gov/sites/default/files/2026-06/cbp_form_5106.pdf
6. Customs Bond, U.S. Customs and Border Protection. Bought from a CBP-approved surety, usually through your customs broker, who files it electronically. A continuous bond covers a year of entries. Fee: Varies. https://www.cbp.gov/sites/default/files/2024-05/cbp_form_301.pdf
7. Product safety certificate, filed electronically at entry, U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission. The importer issues the certificate itself (there is no government form) and, under the eFiling rule, files the certificate data with CBP at entry. Fee: Free. https://www.cpsc.gov/eFiling
8. Unemployment tax account, Texas Workforce Commission. Register online once you pay wages in Texas. Fee: Free. https://www.twc.texas.gov/services/register-tax
9. Certificate of Occupancy, City of Austin Development Services. Needed when the space's use changes or after construction; it may include a site plan exemption and building plan review. For a food business it comes through Austin Public Health's pre-opening inspection. Fee: Varies. https://www.austintexas.gov/development-services/small-business-permitting
10. Sign permit, City of Austin Development Services. Any outdoor sign (wall, awning, projecting, freestanding, roof) needs a permit, applied for on the AB+C portal. Fee: Varies. https://abc.austintexas.gov
11. Franchise tax annual report, Texas Comptroller of Public Accounts. Filed every year by May 15, even when no tax is due. Fee: Free. https://comptroller.texas.gov/taxes/franchise/

### Importers and online sellers in Austin
https://placetta.com/guides/austin/importer-ecommerce.html
1. Application for Employer Identification Number (EIN), Internal Revenue Service. Owners with an SSN or ITIN apply online. A company whose responsible party has neither (most China-based owners) faxes or mails Form SS-4, or calls the IRS international line. Fee: Free. https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/fss4.pdf

4. Texas Sales and Use Tax Permit Application, Texas Comptroller of Public Accounts. Apply online in eSystems before your first sale; one permit for each location. Fee: Free. https://comptroller.texas.gov/taxes/permit/
5. Create/Update Importer Identity Form, U.S. Customs and Border Protection. Sent to CBP (usually through your customs broker), or created in the ACE portal. Needed before your first entry as importer of record. Fee: Free. https://www.cbp.gov/sites/default/files/2026-06/cbp_form_5106.pdf
6. Customs Bond, U.S. Customs and Border Protection. Bought from a CBP-approved surety, usually through your customs broker, who files it electronically. A continuous bond covers a year of entries. Fee: Varies. https://www.cbp.gov/sites/default/files/2024-05/cbp_form_301.pdf
7. ACE Secure Data Portal account for importers, U.S. Customs and Border Protection. Applied for online in ACE. Lets you see your entries, duties and bond. Fee: Free. https://www.cbp.gov/trade/automated/getting-started/portal-applying
8. Product safety certificate, filed electronically at entry, U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission. The importer issues the certificate itself (there is no government form) and, under the eFiling rule, files the certificate data with CBP at entry. Fee: Free. https://www.cpsc.gov/eFiling
9. Franchise tax annual report, Texas Comptroller of Public Accounts. Filed every year by May 15, even when no tax is due. Fee: Free. https://comptroller.texas.gov/taxes/franchise/

9. Unemployment tax account, Texas Workforce Commission. Register online once you pay wages in Texas. Fee: Free. https://www.twc.texas.gov/services/register-tax
10. Certificate of Occupancy, City of Austin Development Services. Needed when the space's use changes or after construction; it may include a site plan exemption and building plan review. For a food business it comes through Austin Public Health's pre-opening inspection. Fee: Varies. https://www.austintexas.gov/development-services/small-business-permitting
11. Hazardous materials storage permit, City of Austin Development Services. Needed to store or use hazardous materials above ground (including large battery stock). Applied for on the AB+C portal. Fee: Varies. https://abc.austintexas.gov
12. Franchise tax annual report, Texas Comptroller of Public Accounts. Filed every year by May 15, even when no tax is due. Fee: Free. https://comptroller.texas.gov/taxes/franchise/

### Milk tea and bubble tea shops in Washington, DC
https://placetta.com/guides/washington-dc/milk-tea-shop.html
1. Application for Employer Identification Number (EIN), Internal Revenue Service. Owners with an SSN or ITIN apply online. A company whose responsible party has neither (most China-based owners) faxes or mails Form SS-4, or calls the IRS international line. Fee: Free. https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/fss4.pdf
2. DC tax registration, DC Office of Tax and Revenue. Register with the Office of Tax and Revenue on the FR-500. Every basic business license applicant must be registered and in good standing, and the license application checks the tax number for Clean Hands. Fee: Varies. https://mytax.dc.gov
3. DC certified food protection manager card, DC Health. A manager who passed a nationally recognized food safety exam applies for DC Health's ID card with a copy of the certificate, in person at 899 North Capitol Street NE or by mail. DLCP asks for the DC Health food manager's certificate with the food license, and a certified manager has to be on duty whenever the place is open. Fee: Varies. https://doh.dc.gov/sites/default/files/dc/sites/doh/publication/attachments/Application%20for%20ID%20Cards.pdf
4. Unemployment insurance employer registration, DC Department of Employment Services, UI Tax Division. Any business with employees working in DC registers online in the Employer Self-Service Portal, which also takes the wage reports and tax payments. Fee: Varies. https://essp.does.dc.gov
5. Food establishment plan review, DC Health, Food Safety and Hygiene Inspection Services Division. Needed before building, converting or remodeling a food establishment, or changing its type of food operation. Plans, specifications and the menu go to DC Health through ProjectDox with the building permit application. Fee: Varies. https://dchealth.dc.gov/sites/default/files/dc/sites/doh/publication/attachments/FS%28redtop%29%20-%20Plan%20review%202018%20v2.pdf
6. Certificate of Occupancy, DC Department of Buildings. Needed when a new owner or tenant takes over a space, even with the same use, and when the space is used for something new; a new use also needs building permits and final inspections. Applied for online in Certifi. Fee: Varies. https://dob.dc.gov/sites/default/files/dc/sites/dob/Certificate%20of%20Occupancy--A%20Quick%20Guide.pdf
7. Food services business license, DC Department of Licensing and Consumer Protection, with DC Health. The basic business license for restaurants, delis, caterers and other food businesses. Apply online in BOSS with the Certificate of Occupancy, the DC Health food manager's certificate, the approved DC Health inspection report, tax registration and Clean Hands, and corporate registration if you have one; pick only the category the business was approved for. Fee: $99. https://boss.dc.gov

6. Cosmetic product facility registration (MoCRA), U.S. Food and Drug Administration. Filed online in Cosmetics Direct by the facility that makes or processes the cosmetics. Fee: Free. https://www.fda.gov/cosmetics/registration-listing-cosmetic-product-facilities-and-products
7. Cosmetic product listing (MoCRA), U.S. Food and Drug Administration. Filed online in Cosmetics Direct by the brand (the responsible person on the label), one listing per product. Fee: Free. https://www.fda.gov/cosmetics/registration-listing-cosmetic-product-facilities-and-products
8. Product safety certificate, filed electronically at entry, U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission. The importer issues the certificate itself (there is no government form) and, under the eFiling rule, files the certificate data with CBP at entry. Fee: Free. https://www.cpsc.gov/eFiling
9. Unemployment insurance employer registration, DC Department of Employment Services, UI Tax Division. Any business with employees working in DC registers online in the Employer Self-Service Portal, which also takes the wage reports and tax payments. Fee: Varies. https://essp.does.dc.gov
10. Certificate of Occupancy, DC Department of Buildings. Needed when a new owner or tenant takes over a space, even with the same use, and when the space is used for something new; a new use also needs building permits and final inspections. Applied for online in Certifi. Fee: Varies. https://dob.dc.gov/sites/default/files/dc/sites/dob/Certificate%20of%20Occupancy--A%20Quick%20Guide.pdf

A company whose responsible party has neither (most China-based owners) faxes or mails Form SS-4, or calls the IRS international line. Fee: Free. https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/fss4.pdf
2. LLC formation, Georgia Secretary of State, Corporations. Form the LLC or register a foreign company online. Fee: Varies. https://ecorp.sos.ga.gov
3. Sales tax registration, Georgia Department of Revenue. Register for sales and withholding tax online. Fee: Free. https://gtc.dor.ga.gov
4. Certified food safety manager, Georgia Department of Public Health, Environmental Health. At least one employee with supervisory and management duties passes an accredited food safety manager exam, and is designated to this one place only. A new food service establishment has 60 days from its permit to employ one, and tells the county within 30 days if it loses its manager. Fee: Varies. https://dph.georgia.gov/node/146
5. Atlanta business license, City of Atlanta, Department of Finance, Office of Revenue. Every business location inside city limits registers. Apply on the city's ATLBiz portal with a government photo ID, the articles of incorporation, notarized SAVE and E-Verify affidavits and the EIN; the city runs the zoning review itself, and some kinds of business also upload a regulatory permit. Fee: Varies. https://atlbiz.atlantaga.gov/_/
6. Food service plan review, Fulton County Board of Health, Environmental Health Services. Before building or extensively remodeling, mail or bring the application, scaled plans, equipment specifications and the fee to the Environmental Health district office nearest the restaurant. An Atlanta address in DeKalb County applies to the DeKalb County Board of Health instead. Fee: Varies. https://FultonCountyGa.gov/-/media/Departments/Board-of-Health/Environmental-Health/Restaurant-Inspection/Link-List-Items/Food-Service-Application.pdf
7. Food service permit, Fulton County Board of Health, Environmental Health Services. Issued by the county once the application and fee are in, the plans are approved and the place passes its pre-opening inspection; apply by mail or in person at the district office nearest the restaurant. An Atlanta address in DeKalb County gets its permit from the DeKalb County Board of Health instead. Fee: Varies. https://fultoncountyga.gov/Inside-Fulton-County/Fulton-County-Departments/Board-of-Health/Environmental-Health/Restaurant-Inspection

6. Product safety certificate, filed electronically at entry, U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission. The importer issues the certificate itself (there is no government form) and, under the eFiling rule, files the certificate data with CBP at entry. Fee: Free. https://www.cpsc.gov/eFiling
7. Atlanta business license, City of Atlanta, Department of Finance, Office of Revenue. Every business location inside city limits registers. Apply on the city's ATLBiz portal with a government photo ID, the articles of incorporation, notarized SAVE and E-Verify affidavits and the EIN; the city runs the zoning review itself, and some kinds of business also upload a regulatory permit. Fee: Varies. https://atlbiz.atlantaga.gov/_/

### Importers and online sellers in Atlanta
https://placetta.com/guides/atlanta/importer-ecommerce.html
1. Application for Employer Identification Number (EIN), Internal Revenue Service. Owners with an SSN or ITIN apply online. A company whose responsible party has neither (most China-based owners) faxes or mails Form SS-4, or calls the IRS international line. Fee: Free. https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/fss4.pdf
2. LLC formation, Georgia Secretary of State, Corporations. Form the LLC or register a foreign company online. Fee: Varies. https://ecorp.sos.ga.gov
3. Create/Update Importer Identity Form, U.S. Customs and Border Protection. Sent to CBP (usually through your customs broker), or created in the ACE portal. Needed before your first entry as importer of record. Fee: Free. https://www.cbp.gov/sites/default/files/2026-06/cbp_form_5106.pdf
4. Sales tax registration, Georgia Department of Revenue. Register for sales and withholding tax online. Fee: Free. https://gtc.dor.ga.gov
5. Customs Bond, U.S. Customs and Border Protection. Bought from a CBP-approved surety, usually through your customs broker, who files it electronically. A continuous bond covers a year of entries. Fee: Varies. https://www.cbp.gov/sites/default/files/2024-05/cbp_form_301.pdf
6. ACE Secure Data Portal account for importers, U.S. Customs and Border Protection. Applied for online in ACE. Lets you see your entries, duties and bond. Fee: Free. https://www.cbp.gov/trade/automated/getting-started/portal-applying
7. Product safety certificate, filed electronically at entry, U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission. The importer issues the certificate itself (there is no government form) and, under the eFiling rule, files the certificate data with CBP at entry. Fee: Free. https://www.cpsc.gov/eFiling
8. Atlanta business license, City of Atlanta, Department of Finance, Office of Revenue. Every business location inside city limits registers. Apply on the city's ATLBiz portal with a government photo ID, the articles of incorporation, notarized SAVE and E-Verify affidavits and the EIN; the city runs the zoning review itself, and some kinds of business also upload a regulatory permit. Fee: Varies. https://atlbiz.atlantaga.gov/_/

### Milk tea and bubble tea shops in Philadelphia
https://placetta.com/guides/philadelphia/milk-tea-shop.html
1. Application for Employer Identification Number (EIN), Internal Revenue Service. Owners with an SSN or ITIN apply online. A company whose responsible party has neither (most China-based owners) faxes or mails Form SS-4, or calls the IRS international line. Fee: Free. https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/fss4.pdf
2. LLC formation, Pennsylvania Department of State. Form the LLC or register a foreign company online. Fee: $125. https://file.dos.pa.gov
3. Pennsylvania tax registration (sales tax license and employer accounts), Pennsylvania Department of Revenue. Register in myPATH (new customers don't need to log in) for sales, use and hotel occupancy tax, employer withholding and unemployment compensation. Fee: Varies. https://mypath.pa.gov/_/
4. Philadelphia food safety certificate, Philadelphia Department of Public Health, Environmental Health Services. Every food business has at least one person certified in food safety at all times. Take a food manager safety course with an approved provider, send the training certificate to the Health Department for checking, then apply for the city certificate online, or in person or by mail with a money order. Fee: $30. https://philadph.formstack.com/forms/fscapp
5. Philadelphia tax account (BIRT and Wage Tax), City of Philadelphia Department of Revenue. Register the business as a new taxpayer on the Philadelphia Tax Center to get a Philadelphia Tax Identification Number, used for the Business Income and Receipts Tax and, with staff, the Wage Tax. The paper application can also apply for the Commercial Activity License. Fee: Varies. https://tax-services.phila.gov/
6. Commercial activity license, City of Philadelphia, Department of Licenses and Inspections. Every person or company doing business in Philadelphia needs it, and should get it before any other business license. Apply in eCLIPSE with the EIN and the BIRT ID, under the legal name on the city tax account, or at the Permit and License Center by appointment. Fee: Free. https://eclipse.phila.gov/
7. Food business plan review, Philadelphia Department of Public Health, Office of Food Protection. Anyone opening a stationary food business applies after zoning is approved and before construction or installing food equipment. Call 215-685-7495 to submit, book an appointment or walk in at 7801 Essington Ave (weekdays 9 a.m. to 1 p.m.). The application covers 13 items, from the site plan to the menu, with a copy of the city food safety certificate. Fee: Varies. https://phila.gov/media/20250423122123/Plan-Review-for-Stationary-Food-Businesses-2025-fillable.pdf
8. Food preparation and serving license, City of Philadelphia, Department of Licenses and Inspections. For any business that prepares or serves food to the public. Apply in eCLIPSE with the BIRT ID, the Commercial Activity License, proof of occupancy (a license for the same use in the last 3 years, or zoning approval) and the Health Department's License Eligibility Report dated within 30 days. Fee: Varies. https://eclipse.phila.gov/

4. Create/Update Importer Identity Form, U.S. Customs and Border Protection. Sent to CBP (usually through your customs broker), or created in the ACE portal. Needed before your first entry as importer of record. Fee: Free. https://www.cbp.gov/sites/default/files/2026-06/cbp_form_5106.pdf
5. Customs Bond, U.S. Customs and Border Protection. Bought from a CBP-approved surety, usually through your customs broker, who files it electronically. A continuous bond covers a year of entries. Fee: Varies. https://www.cbp.gov/sites/default/files/2024-05/cbp_form_301.pdf
6. Philadelphia tax account (BIRT and Wage Tax), City of Philadelphia Department of Revenue. Register the business as a new taxpayer on the Philadelphia Tax Center to get a Philadelphia Tax Identification Number, used for the Business Income and Receipts Tax and, with staff, the Wage Tax. The paper application can also apply for the Commercial Activity License. Fee: Varies. https://tax-services.phila.gov/
7. Product safety certificate, filed electronically at entry, U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission. The importer issues the certificate itself (there is no government form) and, under the eFiling rule, files the certificate data with CBP at entry. Fee: Free. https://www.cpsc.gov/eFiling
8. Commercial activity license, City of Philadelphia, Department of Licenses and Inspections. Every person or company doing business in Philadelphia needs it, and should get it before any other business license. Apply in eCLIPSE with the EIN and the BIRT ID, under the legal name on the city tax account, or at the Permit and License Center by appointment. Fee: Free. https://eclipse.phila.gov/

### Milk tea and bubble tea shops in Las Vegas
https://placetta.com/guides/las-vegas/milk-tea-shop.html
1. Application for Employer Identification Number (EIN), Internal Revenue Service. Owners with an SSN or ITIN apply online. A company whose responsible party has neither (most China-based owners) faxes or mails Form SS-4, or calls the IRS international line. Fee: Free. https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/fss4.pdf
2. LLC formation and state business license, Nevada Secretary of State (SilverFlume). Form the company and get the state business license together online. Fee: Varies. https://www.nvsilverflume.gov
3. Nevada sales tax permit, Nevada Department of Taxation. Register online in My Nevada Tax once you have an EIN and the state business license, or mail the Nevada Business Registration Form. Businesses paying more than $50,000 in wages in a quarter also register for the Modified Business Tax, through DETR. Fee: $15. https://mynvtax.nv.gov/tap/_/
4. Food handler cards for staff, Southern Nevada Health District. Everyone employed in or running a food establishment holds one. A first card means an in-person test at a Health District location with photo ID; some renewals can be done online. A Certified Food Safety Manager card also meets the requirement. Fee: $20. https://www.southernnevadahealthdistrict.org/?p=3661
5. City of Las Vegas business license, City of Las Vegas, Business Licensing. For an address inside City of Las Vegas limits; check the jurisdiction first, since other addresses license with Clark County or their own city. Confirm the zoning allows the business and the building is code compliant, get the state business license and register with the Department of Taxation, then apply on the city's online portal. Fee: Varies. https://www.lasvegasnevada.gov/dashboard
6. Clark County business license, Clark County Business License. For an address in unincorporated Clark County. Confirm the zoning allows the activity, get the state business license, register with the Department of Taxation, file a fictitious firm name with the County Clerk if you trade under another name, and finish all construction; then apply online or at 500 S Grand Central Pkwy, 3rd floor, with proof of rights to the location and, for food, proof of your Health District application. Fee: Varies. https://blepay.clarkcountynv.gov/NAICSDefault.aspx
7. Unemployment insurance employer account, Nevada Department of Employment, Training and Rehabilitation, Employment Security Division. Employers open their unemployment insurance account with DETR's Employment Security Division, whose Registration Unit handles Nevada business registration; DETR shares the details with the Department of Taxation. The account is then managed in the Employer Self-Service portal. Fee: Varies. http://nui.nv.gov/ess
8. Food establishment plan review, Southern Nevada Health District. Plans are needed for new and remodeled places and must be approved before construction starts. Email the application packet, plans in PDF, the menu, the food questionnaire and proof of the lease or deed to FOODREV@SNHD.ORG; a remote plan review follows and the invoice comes by email. Two construction walkthroughs are included. Fee: Varies. https://media.southernnevadahealthdistrict.org/download/eh/2022/plan-review/applications/snhd-application-packet-food-202207.pdf
9. Food establishment health permit, Southern Nevada Health District. Issued after the final permitting inspection, which needs a Certificate of Occupancy (or a temporary one) after new construction or a remodel, and every fee paid first. Food can't be stocked until the permit is approved. Fee: Varies. https://media.southernnevadahealthdistrict.org/download/eh/2022/plan-review/applications/snhd-application-packet-food-202207.pdf

7. Unemployment insurance employer account, Nevada Department of Employment, Training and Rehabilitation, Employment Security Division. Employers open their unemployment insurance account with DETR's Employment Security Division, whose Registration Unit handles Nevada business registration; DETR shares the details with the Department of Taxation. The account is then managed in the Employer Self-Service portal. Fee: Varies. http://nui.nv.gov/ess
8. Food establishment health permit, Southern Nevada Health District. Issued after the final permitting inspection, which needs a Certificate of Occupancy (or a temporary one) after new construction or a remodel, and every fee paid first. Food can't be stocked until the permit is approved. Fee: Varies. https://media.southernnevadahealthdistrict.org/download/eh/2022/plan-review/applications/snhd-application-packet-food-202207.pdf

8. Product safety certificate, filed electronically at entry, U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission. The importer issues the certificate itself (there is no government form) and, under the eFiling rule, files the certificate data with CBP at entry. Fee: Free. https://www.cpsc.gov/eFiling
9. City of Las Vegas business license, City of Las Vegas, Business Licensing. For an address inside City of Las Vegas limits; check the jurisdiction first, since other addresses license with Clark County or their own city. ### Milk tea and bubble tea shops in San Antonio
https://placetta.com/guides/san-antonio/milk-tea-shop.html
1. Application for Employer Identification Number (EIN), Internal Revenue Service. Owners with an SSN or ITIN apply online. A company whose responsible party has neither (most China-based owners) faxes or mails Form SS-4, or calls the IRS international line. Fee: Free. https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/fss4.pdf
2. Certificate of Formation (Texas LLC), Texas Secretary of State. Filed online in SOSDirect, or by mail or fax. Fee: $300. https://www.sos.state.tx.us/corp/forms/205_boc.pdf
3. Assumed Name Certificate (DBA), Texas Secretary of State. Filed when the store trades under a name other than the legal name. Fee: $25. https://www.sos.state.tx.us/corp/forms/503_boc.pdf
4. Texas Sales and Use Tax Permit Application, Texas Comptroller of Public Accounts. Apply online in eSystems before your first sale; one permit for each location. Fee: Free. https://comptroller.texas.gov/taxes/permit/
5. Certified food manager, Texas Department of State Health Services. At least one manager passes an exam from a DSHS-licensed certified food manager program. Local health departments require a certified food manager on site whenever the place is open. Fee: Varies. https://www.dshs.texas.gov/food-managers
6. Food handler certificates for staff, Texas Department of State Health Services. Every employee who works with unpackaged food, equipment or food-contact surfaces finishes an accredited food handler course within 30 days of hire. Certified food managers are exempt. Fee: Varies. https://www.dshs.texas.gov/food-handlers
7. Unemployment tax account, Texas Workforce Commission. Register online once you pay wages in Texas. Fee: Free. https://www.twc.texas.gov/services/register-tax
8. Certificate of Occupancy, City of San Antonio Development Services. Needed when the new business is a different type of business than the one in the building now; a new owner or tenant with the same use only updates the name on the existing certificate. Expect building, electrical, mechanical, plumbing and fire inspections. Fee: Varies. https://www.sanantonio.gov/DSD/Business/CofO
9. Food establishment license, San Antonio Metropolitan Health District (Metro Health). Once the space is zoned for the use and the Certificate of Occupancy requirements are complete, buy the license at the Development and Business Services Center, 1901 S. Alamo. Fee: Varies. https://www.sanantonio.gov/Health/FoodLicensing/FAQs
10. Franchise tax annual report, Texas Comptroller of Public Accounts. Filed every year by May 15, even when no tax is due. Fee: Free. https://comptroller.texas.gov/taxes/franchise/

3. Assumed Name Certificate (DBA), Texas Secretary of State. Filed when the store trades under a name other than the legal name. Fee: $25. https://www.sos.state.tx.us/corp/forms/503_boc.pdf
4. Texas Sales and Use Tax Permit Application, Texas Comptroller of Public Accounts. Apply online in eSystems before your first sale; one permit for each location. Fee: Free. https://comptroller.texas.gov/taxes/permit/
5. Certified food manager, Texas Department of State Health Services. At least one manager passes an exam from a DSHS-licensed certified food manager program. Local health departments require a certified food manager on site whenever the place is open. Fee: Varies. https://www.dshs.texas.gov/food-managers
6. Food handler certificates for staff, Texas Department of State Health Services. Every employee who works with unpackaged food, equipment or food-contact surfaces finishes an accredited food handler course within 30 days of hire. Certified food managers are exempt. Fee: Varies. https://www.dshs.texas.gov/food-handlers
7. Unemployment tax account, Texas Workforce Commission. Register online once you pay wages in Texas. Fee: Free. https://www.twc.texas.gov/services/register-tax
8. Certificate of Occupancy, City of San Antonio Development Services. Needed when the new business is a different type of business than the one in the building now; a new owner or tenant with the same use only updates the name on the existing certificate. Expect building, electrical, mechanical, plumbing and fire inspections. Fee: Varies. https://www.sanantonio.gov/DSD/Business/CofO
9. Food establishment license, San Antonio Metropolitan Health District (Metro Health). Once the space is zoned for the use and the Certificate of Occupancy requirements are complete, buy the license at the Development and Business Services Center, 1901 S. Alamo. Fee: Varies. https://www.sanantonio.gov/Health/FoodLicensing/FAQs
10. Franchise tax annual report, Texas Comptroller of Public Accounts. Filed every year by May 15, even when no tax is due. Fee: Free. https://comptroller.texas.gov/taxes/franchise/

5. Create/Update Importer Identity Form, U.S. Customs and Border Protection. Sent to CBP (usually through your customs broker), or created in the ACE portal. Needed before your first entry as importer of record. Fee: Free. https://www.cbp.gov/sites/default/files/2026-06/cbp_form_5106.pdf
6. Customs Bond, U.S. Customs and Border Protection. Bought from a CBP-approved surety, usually through your customs broker, who files it electronically. A continuous bond covers a year of entries. Fee: Varies. https://www.cbp.gov/sites/default/files/2024-05/cbp_form_301.pdf
7. Cosmetic product facility registration (MoCRA), U.S. Food and Drug Administration. Filed online in Cosmetics Direct by the facility that makes or processes the cosmetics. Fee: Free. https://www.fda.gov/cosmetics/registration-listing-cosmetic-product-facilities-and-products
8. Cosmetic product listing (MoCRA), U.S. Food and Drug Administration. Filed online in Cosmetics Direct by the brand (the responsible person on the label), one listing per product. Fee: Free. https://www.fda.gov/cosmetics/registration-listing-cosmetic-product-facilities-and-products
9. Product safety certificate, filed electronically at entry, U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission. The importer issues the certificate itself (there is no government form) and, under the eFiling rule, files the certificate data with CBP at entry. Fee: Free. https://www.cpsc.gov/eFiling
10. Unemployment tax account, Texas Workforce Commission. Register online once you pay wages in Texas. Fee: Free. https://www.twc.texas.gov/services/register-tax

### Milk tea and bubble tea shops in Tampa
https://placetta.com/guides/tampa/milk-tea-shop.html
1. Application for Employer Identification Number (EIN), Internal Revenue Service. Owners with an SSN or ITIN apply online. A company whose responsible party has neither (most China-based owners) faxes or mails Form SS-4, or calls the IRS international line. Fee: Free. https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/fss4.pdf
2. LLC formation, Florida Division of Corporations (Sunbiz). Form the LLC or register a foreign company online. Fee: $125. https://dos.fl.gov/sunbiz/
3. Florida sales tax and reemployment tax registration, Florida Department of Revenue. Register online before you start doing business. The same application covers sales and use tax and reemployment tax, Florida's unemployment tax for employers. Fee: Varies. https://floridarevenue.com/taxes/registration
4. Certified food protection manager, Florida DBPR, Division of Hotels and Restaurants. Food managers complete training and pass a certification exam from an accredited program within 30 days of starting the job, and the restaurant shows proof whenever an inspector asks. Fee: Varies. https://www2.myfloridalicense.com/hotels-restaurants/food-lodging/food-manager/
5. Hillsborough County local business tax receipt, Hillsborough County Tax Collector. Get it before you start trading: apply online in BTExpress in one sitting, with the business name, SSN or EIN, a physical county address and any state or county license the business needs. Fee: Varies. https://www.hillstaxfl.gov/taxes/business-tax-services/new-regulated-businesses/
6. City of Tampa business tax receipt, City of Tampa Business Tax. A business inside Tampa city limits files the new business application online; the city may inspect the site. Fee: Varies. https://www.tampa.gov/service/new-business-tax-receipt-application
7. Food service plan review, Florida DBPR, Division of Hotels and Restaurants. Required for a space that is newly built, remodeled, converted from another use or reopening after 18 months closed; the state recommends approval before construction. Submit the plan with labeled equipment and a sample menu together with the new license application on DBPR Online. Fee: Free. https://www.myfloridalicense.com/intentions2.asp?chBoard=true&SID=&boardid=200&professionid=2010
8. Florida public food service license, Florida DBPR, Division of Hotels and Restaurants. Apply and pay on DBPR Online, one license for each operation. Once the plan review requirements are met, call 850-487-1395 several business days before opening to book the opening inspection; serve nobody until it passes and a temporary paper license is issued on the spot. Fee: Varies. https://www.myfloridalicense.com/intentions2.asp?chBoard=true&SID=&boardid=200&professionid=2010

Submit the plan with labeled equipment and a sample menu together with the new license application on DBPR Online. Fee: Free. https://www.myfloridalicense.com/intentions2.asp?chBoard=true&SID=&boardid=200&professionid=2010
8. Florida public food service license, Florida DBPR, Division of Hotels and Restaurants. Apply and pay on DBPR Online, one license for each operation. Once the plan review requirements are met, call 850-487-1395 several business days before opening to book the opening inspection; serve nobody until it passes and a temporary paper license is issued on the spot. Fee: Varies. https://www.myfloridalicense.com/intentions2.asp?chBoard=true&SID=&boardid=200&professionid=2010

4. Create/Update Importer Identity Form, U.S. Customs and Border Protection. Sent to CBP (usually through your customs broker), or created in the ACE portal. Needed before your first entry as importer of record. Fee: Free. https://www.cbp.gov/sites/default/files/2026-06/cbp_form_5106.pdf
5. Customs Bond, U.S. Customs and Border Protection. Bought from a CBP-approved surety, usually through your customs broker, who files it electronically. A continuous bond covers a year of entries. Fee: Varies. https://www.cbp.gov/sites/default/files/2024-05/cbp_form_301.pdf
6. Cosmetic product facility registration (MoCRA), U.S. Food and Drug Administration. Filed online in Cosmetics Direct by the facility that makes or processes the cosmetics. Fee: Free. https://www.fda.gov/cosmetics/registration-listing-cosmetic-product-facilities-and-products
7. Cosmetic product listing (MoCRA), U.S. Food and Drug Administration. Filed online in Cosmetics Direct by the brand (the responsible person on the label), one listing per product. Fee: Free. https://www.fda.gov/cosmetics/registration-listing-cosmetic-product-facilities-and-products
8. Product safety certificate, filed electronically at entry, U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission. The importer issues the certificate itself (there is no government form) and, under the eFiling rule, files the certificate data with CBP at entry. Fee: Free. https://www.cpsc.gov/eFiling
9. Hillsborough County local business tax receipt, Hillsborough County Tax Collector. Get it before you start trading: apply online in BTExpress in one sitting, with the business name, SSN or EIN, a physical county address and any state or county license the business needs. ### Milk tea and bubble tea shops in San Diego
https://placetta.com/guides/san-diego/milk-tea-shop.html
1. Application for Employer Identification Number (EIN), Internal Revenue Service. Owners with an SSN or ITIN apply online. A company whose responsible party has neither (most China-based owners) faxes or mails Form SS-4, or calls the IRS international line. Fee: Free. https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/fss4.pdf
2. Articles of Organization (California LLC), California Secretary of State. Filed online in bizfile Online. Fee: $70. https://bizfileonline.sos.ca.gov/
3. Seller's permit, California Department of Tax and Fee Administration. Register online before your first sale; one permit for each location. Fee: Free. https://onlineservices.cdtfa.ca.gov/
4. Certified food protection manager, California Retail Food Code, enforced by the county or city environmental health department. An owner or employee of a place that prepares, handles or serves unpackaged perishable food passes a food protection manager exam from an accredited organization. A new place, a new owner, or a place that loses its certified person has 60 days to have one, and one person can't be certified for two locations. Keep the certificate on file for the inspector. Fee: Varies. http://publichealth.lacounty.gov/eh/business/certified-food-handler-manager.htm
5. City of San Diego Business Tax Certificate, City of San Diego, Office of the City Treasurer. Every business operating in the City of San Diego registers, online on the Treasurer's portal, by mail or in person by appointment. Late fees apply to applications received 15 days after the business start date. Fee: Varies. https://pay.sandiego.gov/BTaxApp
6. Registration Form for Commercial Employers, California Employment Development Department. Register in e-Services for Business within 15 days of paying over $100 in wages. Fee: Free. https://edd.ca.gov/en/payroll_taxes/save_time_and_register_online/
7. Food facility plan check, County of San Diego Department of Environmental Health and Quality. Submit at least three sets of plans with the application and fee to a DEHQ office; plans are approved before the building permit is issued. Fee: Varies. https://www.sandiegocounty.gov/content/sdc/deh/fhd/food/food_faq.html
8. Certificate of Occupancy, City of San Diego Development Services. Issued after the final inspection of building permit work. Needed for a change of occupancy classification or a tenant improvement in a shell building; not needed for a change of owner or tenant when the occupancy doesn't change. Fee: Varies. https://www.sandiego.gov/development-services/forms-publications/information-bulletin/585
9. Public health permit (food facility), County of San Diego Department of Environmental Health and Quality. Required by law for every retail food facility in San Diego County. Fee: Varies. https://www.sandiegocounty.gov/content/sdc/deh/fhd/food/food_faq.html
10. LLC annual tax ($800), California Franchise Tax Board. Paid every year by every LLC registered or doing business in California. Fee: $800. https://www.ftb.ca.gov/pay/

7. Food facility plan check, County of San Diego Department of Environmental Health and Quality. 1. Application for Employer Identification Number (EIN), Internal Revenue Service. Owners with an SSN or ITIN apply online. A company whose responsible party has neither (most China-based owners) faxes or mails Form SS-4, or calls the IRS international line. Fee: Free. https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/fss4.pdf
2. Articles of Organization (California LLC), California Secretary of State. Filed online in bizfile Online. Fee: $70. https://bizfileonline.sos.ca.gov/
3. Seller's permit, California Department of Tax and Fee Administration. Register online before your first sale; one permit for each location. Fee: Free. https://onlineservices.cdtfa.ca.gov/
4. Certified food protection manager, California Retail Food Code, enforced by the county or city environmental health department. An owner or employee of a place that prepares, handles or serves unpackaged perishable food passes a food protection manager exam from an accredited organization. A new place, a new owner, or a place that loses its certified person has 60 days to have one, and one person can't be certified for two locations. Keep the certificate on file for the inspector. Fee: Varies. http://publichealth.lacounty.gov/eh/business/certified-food-handler-manager.htm
5. City of Irvine business license, City of Irvine Community Development, Business Licensing. A city tax rather than a regulatory license: apply online or at the public counter, confirm first that the use is allowed at the address, and display the license at the business. Fee: Varies. https://cityofirvine.gov/community-development/business-licensing
6. Registration Form for Commercial Employers, California Employment Development Department. Register in e-Services for Business within 15 days of paying over $100 in wages. Fee: Free. https://edd.ca.gov/en/payroll_taxes/save_time_and_register_online/
7. Food facility plan check, Orange County Health Care Agency, Environmental Health. Submit the plan check online with three sets of plans and specifications before construction; the fee is set at conditional approval. Fee: Varies. https://www.ochealthinfo.com/services-programs/environmental-health/plan-check
8. Food facility health permit, Orange County Health Care Agency, Environmental Health. Every food facility that stores, prepares, packages, serves or vends food needs a valid health permit; book inspections 5 working days ahead. Fee: Varies. https://ochealthinfo.com/sites/healthcare/files/2023-04/Food%20Health%20Permit%20Application%20W.pdf
9. LLC annual tax ($800), California Franchise Tax Board. Paid every year by every LLC registered or doing business in California. Fee: $800. https://www.ftb.ca.gov/pay/

### Cosmetics stores in Irvine
https://placetta.com/guides/irvine/cosmetics-store.html
1. Application for Employer Identification Number (EIN), Internal Revenue Service. Owners with an SSN or ITIN apply online. A company whose responsible party has neither (most China-based owners) faxes or mails Form SS-4, or calls the IRS international line. Fee: Free. https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/fss4.pdf
2. Articles of Organization (California LLC), California Secretary of State. Filed online in bizfile Online. Fee: $70. https://bizfileonline.sos.ca.gov/
3. Seller's permit, California Department of Tax and Fee Administration. Register online before your first sale; one permit for each location. Fee: Free. https://onlineservices.cdtfa.ca.gov/
4. Create/Update Importer Identity Form, U.S. Customs and Border Protection. Sent to CBP (usually through your customs broker), or created in the ACE portal. Needed before your first entry as importer of record. Fee: Free. https://www.cbp.gov/sites/default/files/2026-06/cbp_form_5106.pdf
5. Customs Bond, U.S. Customs and Border Protection. Bought from a CBP-approved surety, usually through your customs broker, who files it electronically. A continuous bond covers a year of entries. Fee: Varies. https://www.cbp.gov/sites/default/files/2024-05/cbp_form_301.pdf
6. Cosmetic product facility registration (MoCRA), U.S. Food and Drug Administration. Filed online in Cosmetics Direct by the facility that makes or processes the cosmetics. Fee: Free. https://www.fda.gov/cosmetics/registration-listing-cosmetic-product-facilities-and-products
7. Cosmetic product listing (MoCRA), U.S. Food and Drug Administration. Filed online in Cosmetics Direct by the brand (the responsible person on the label), one listing per product. Fee: Free. https://www.fda.gov/cosmetics/registration-listing-cosmetic-product-facilities-and-products
8. Product safety certificate, filed electronically at entry, U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission. The importer issues the certificate itself (there is no government form) and, under the eFiling rule, files the certificate data with CBP at entry. Fee: Free. https://www.cpsc.gov/eFiling
9. City of Irvine business license, City of Irvine Community Development, Business Licensing. A city tax rather than a regulatory license: apply online or at the public counter, confirm first that the use is allowed at the address, and display the license at the business. Fee: Varies. https://cityofirvine.gov/community-development/business-licensing
10. Registration Form for Commercial Employers, California Employment Development Department. Register in e-Services for Business within 15 days of paying over $100 in wages. Fee: Free. https://edd.ca.gov/en/payroll_taxes/save_time_and_register_online/
11. LLC annual tax ($800), California Franchise Tax Board. Paid every year by every LLC registered or doing business in California. Fee: $800. https://www.ftb.ca.gov/pay/
12. Packaging producer registration (EPR), CalRecycle, through Circular Action Alliance. The brand owner or importer of packaged goods sold in California registers and reports with the producer organization. Fee: Varies. https://circularactionalliance.org/california
13. Proposition 65 warning labels, California Office of Environmental Health Hazard Assessment. Nothing is filed. Businesses with 10 or more employees warn before exposing Californians to listed chemicals, including online at checkout. Fee: Free. https://www.p65warnings.ca.gov/business-resources/frequently-asked-questions-businesses

### Milk tea and bubble tea shops in Orlando
https://placetta.com/guides/orlando/milk-tea-shop.html
1. Application for Employer Identification Number (EIN), Internal Revenue Service. Owners with an SSN or ITIN apply online. A company whose responsible party has neither (most China-based owners) faxes or mails Form SS-4, or calls the IRS international line. Fee: Free. https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/fss4.pdf
2. LLC formation, Florida Division of Corporations (Sunbiz). Form the LLC or register a foreign company online. Fee: $125. https://dos.fl.gov/sunbiz/
3. Florida sales tax and reemployment tax registration, Florida Department of Revenue. Register online before you start doing business. The same application covers sales and use tax and reemployment tax, Florida's unemployment tax for employers. Fee: Varies. https://floridarevenue.com/taxes/registration
4. Certified food protection manager, Florida DBPR, Division of Hotels and Restaurants. Food managers complete training and pass a certification exam from an accredited program within 30 days of starting the job, and the restaurant shows proof whenever an inspector asks. Fee: Varies. https://www2.myfloridalicense.com/hotels-restaurants/food-lodging/food-manager/
5. City of Orlando business tax receipt and certificate of use, City of Orlando, Permitting Services. Businesses inside city limits apply online with the Sunbiz registration, EIN and any state license; the certificate of use confirms the zoning allows the business. Get it before the county receipt. Fee: Varies. https://orlando.opencounter.com/permits/business-tax-receipt
6. Orange County (FL) local business tax receipt, Orange County Tax Collector. Apply online or in person after the city receipt, uploading the city receipt, Sunbiz registration, any state license and the EIN. Fee: Varies. https://county-taxes.net/fl-orange/btexpress
7. Food service plan review, Florida DBPR, Division of Hotels and Restaurants. Required for a space that is newly built, remodeled, converted from another use or reopening after 18 months closed; the state recommends approval before construction. Submit the plan with labeled equipment and a sample menu together with the new license application on DBPR Online. Fee: Free. https://www.myfloridalicense.com/intentions2.asp?chBoard=true&SID=&boardid=200&professionid=2010
8. Florida public food service license, Florida DBPR, Division of Hotels and Restaurants. Apply and pay on DBPR Online, one license for each operation. Once the plan review requirements are met, call 850-487-1395 several business days before opening to book the opening inspection; serve nobody until it passes and a temporary paper license is issued on the spot. Fee: Varies. https://www.myfloridalicense.com/intentions2.asp?chBoard=true&SID=&boardid=200&professionid=2010

4. Create/Update Importer Identity Form, U.S. Customs and Border Protection. Sent to CBP (usually through your customs broker), or created in the ACE portal. Needed before your first entry as importer of record. Fee: Free. https://www.cbp.gov/sites/default/files/2026-06/cbp_form_5106.pdf
5. Customs Bond, U.S. Customs and Border Protection. Bought from a CBP-approved surety, usually through your customs broker, who files it electronically. A continuous bond covers a year of entries. Fee: Varies. https://www.cbp.gov/sites/default/files/2024-05/cbp_form_301.pdf
6. Cosmetic product facility registration (MoCRA), U.S. Food and Drug Administration. Filed online in Cosmetics Direct by the facility that makes or processes the cosmetics. Fee: Free. https://www.fda.gov/cosmetics/registration-listing-cosmetic-product-facilities-and-products
7. Cosmetic product listing (MoCRA), U.S. Food and Drug Administration. Filed online in Cosmetics Direct by the brand (the responsible person on the label), one listing per product. Fee: Free. https://www.fda.gov/cosmetics/registration-listing-cosmetic-product-facilities-and-products
8. Product safety certificate, filed electronically at entry, U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission. The importer issues the certificate itself (there is no government form) and, under the eFiling rule, files the certificate data with CBP at entry. Fee: Free. https://www.cpsc.gov/eFiling
9. City of Orlando business tax receipt and certificate of use, City of Orlando, Permitting Services. Businesses inside city limits apply online with the Sunbiz registration, EIN and any state license; the certificate of use confirms the zoning allows the business. Get it before the county receipt. ### Milk tea and bubble tea shops in Fort Worth
https://placetta.com/guides/fort-worth/milk-tea-shop.html
1. Application for Employer Identification Number (EIN), Internal Revenue Service. Owners with an SSN or ITIN apply online. A company whose responsible party has neither (most China-based owners) faxes or mails Form SS-4, or calls the IRS international line. Fee: Free. https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/fss4.pdf
2. Certificate of Formation (Texas LLC), Texas Secretary of State. Filed online in SOSDirect, or by mail or fax. Fee: $300. https://www.sos.state.tx.us/corp/forms/205_boc.pdf
3. Assumed Name Certificate (DBA), Texas Secretary of State. Filed when the store trades under a name other than the legal name. Fee: $25. https://www.sos.state.tx.us/corp/forms/503_boc.pdf
4. Texas Sales and Use Tax Permit Application, Texas Comptroller of Public Accounts. Apply online in eSystems before your first sale; one permit for each location. Fee: Free. https://comptroller.texas.gov/taxes/permit/
5. Certified food manager, Texas Department of State Health Services. At least one manager passes an exam from a DSHS-licensed certified food manager program. Local health departments require a certified food manager on site whenever the place is open. Fee: Varies. https://www.dshs.texas.gov/food-managers
6. Food handler certificates for staff, Texas Department of State Health Services. Every employee who works with unpackaged food, equipment or food-contact surfaces finishes an accredited food handler course within 30 days of hire. Certified food managers are exempt. Fee: Varies. https://www.dshs.texas.gov/food-handlers
7. Unemployment tax account, Texas Workforce Commission. Register online once you pay wages in Texas. Fee: Free. https://www.twc.texas.gov/services/register-tax
8. Food establishment plan review, City of Fort Worth Consumer Health. Needed before a food establishment is built, extensively remodeled or converted; fees are paid before the review starts. Fee: Varies. https://www.fortworthtexas.gov/departments/environmental-services/consumer-health/plan-review
9. Certificate of Occupancy, City of Fort Worth Development Services. Every building used in Fort Worth needs one. Apply on Accela Citizen Access: same use as before is an existing-ordinance permit, a new use is a change of use with plan review. Issued after all final inspections pass. Fee: Varies. https://aca-prod.accela.com/CFW
10. Food establishment permit, City of Fort Worth Consumer Health. Issued by Consumer Health after the Certificate of Occupancy and a permit inspection, before any food preparation starts. Fee: Varies. https://www.fortworthtexas.gov/departments/environmental-services/consumer-health/plan-review
11. Franchise tax annual report, Texas Comptroller of Public Accounts. Filed every year by May 15, even when no tax is due. Fee: Free. https://comptroller.texas.gov/taxes/franchise/

9. Product safety certificate, filed electronically at entry, U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission. The importer issues the certificate itself (there is no government form) and, under the eFiling rule, files the certificate data with CBP at entry. Fee: Free. https://www.cpsc.gov/eFiling

### Milk tea and bubble tea shops in Phoenix
https://placetta.com/guides/phoenix/milk-tea-shop.html
1. Application for Employer Identification Number (EIN), Internal Revenue Service. Owners with an SSN or ITIN apply online. A company whose responsible party has neither (most China-based owners) faxes or mails Form SS-4, or calls the IRS international line. Fee: Free. https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/fss4.pdf
2. Arizona LLC formation, Arizona Corporation Commission. File the Articles of Organization online, by mail or in person. Publication is required: if the statutory agent is in Maricopa or Pima County the Commission publishes it, otherwise publish a notice in a newspaper. Fee: Varies. https://www.azcc.gov/docs/default-source/corps-files/forms/l010-articles-of-organization.pdf
3. Transaction privilege tax (TPT) license, Arizona Department of Revenue. A business selling taxable products or services gets a license for each location, online on AZTaxes.gov or with the paper JT-1. The same application registers employers with the Department of Economic Security for unemployment insurance. Fee: Varies. https://azdor.gov/transaction-privilege-tax/tpt-license/applying-tpt-license
4. Food establishment plan review, Maricopa County Environmental Services. Apply in the county Permit Center with the supporting documents before construction starts; the county advises applying 6 to 8 weeks ahead. Fee: Varies. https://maricopacountyaz-energovweb.tylerhost.net/apps/selfservice#/home
5. Building permit and Certificate of Occupancy, City of Phoenix Planning and Development. Tenant improvements of a newly occupied space or a change of occupancy go through plan review; the Certificate of Occupancy is generated once all inspections pass and stays with the address. Phoenix doesn't issue a general business license. Fee: Varies. https://www.phoenix.gov/administration/departments/pdd/commercial-multifamily-building/commercial-process-overview.html
6. Food establishment permit, Maricopa County Environmental Services. Apply in the county Permit Center; after the final inspection, pay the annual permit fee to receive the permit and open. Fee: Varies. https://maricopacountyaz-energovweb.tylerhost.net/apps/selfservice#/home

### Milk tea and bubble tea shops in Oakland
https://placetta.com/guides/oakland/milk-tea-shop.html
1. Application for Employer Identification Number (EIN), Internal Revenue Service. Owners with an SSN or ITIN apply online. A company whose responsible party has neither (most China-based owners) faxes or mails Form SS-4, or calls the IRS international line. Fee: Free. https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/fss4.pdf
2. Articles of Organization (California LLC), California Secretary of State. Filed online in bizfile Online. Fee: $70. https://bizfileonline.sos.ca.gov/
3. Seller's permit, California Department of Tax and Fee Administration. Register online before your first sale; one permit for each location. Fee: Free. https://onlineservices.cdtfa.ca.gov/
4. Certified food protection manager, California Retail Food Code, enforced by the county or city environmental health department. An owner or employee of a place that prepares, handles or serves unpackaged perishable food passes a food protection manager exam from an accredited organization. A new place, a new owner, or a place that loses its certified person has 60 days to have one, and one person can't be certified for two locations. Keep the certificate on file for the inspector. Fee: Varies. http://publichealth.lacounty.gov/eh/business/certified-food-handler-manager.htm
5. Oakland zoning clearance, City of Oakland Planning and Building Department. Every business operating in Oakland gets one for its location before the business tax certificate, and again when it moves or changes owner. Apply in the city's Online Permit Center with the street address, parcel number and a description of the business; payment is due when you submit. Some uses first need a conditional use permit. Fee: Varies. https://aca-prod.accela.com/OAKLAND/urlrouting.ashx?type=1002&IsSkipDisclaimer=Y&module=Planning&CAPType=Planning/Applications/Counter/Zoning+Clearance
6. City of Oakland business tax certificate, City of Oakland Finance Department, Business Tax Office. Apply online or at the Business Tax Office, listing the zoning clearance and, if you sell goods, the California seller's permit. Fees are due within 30 days of the business start date. Fee: Varies. https://oakland.hdlgov.com/
7. Registration Form for Commercial Employers, California Employment Development Department. Register in e-Services for Business within 15 days of paying over $100 in wages. Fee: Free. https://edd.ca.gov/en/payroll_taxes/save_time_and_register_online/
8. Food facility plan check, Alameda County Environmental Health Department. Plans must be approved before any new construction or remodel starts. Bring one set of plans drawn at 1/4 inch per foot with equipment spec sheets, the menu, the water heater and hood worksheets, and the plan check questionnaire and worksheet with payment to 1131 Harbor Bay Parkway, Alameda. After approval, three sets are stamped and two go to the city for the building permits. Fee: Varies. https://health.alamedacountyca.gov/alameda-county-plan-check-guide-for-retail-food-facilities/
9. Health permit to operate a food facility, Alameda County Environmental Health Department. After the rough plumbing, pre-final and final inspections (book each at least 48 hours ahead), complete the permit application; the permit is issued once the fees are paid. Fee: Varies. https://health.alamedacountyca.gov/alameda-county-plan-check-guide-for-retail-food-facilities/
10. LLC annual tax ($800), California Franchise Tax Board. Paid every year by every LLC registered or doing business in California. Fee: $800. https://www.ftb.ca.gov/pay/

Apply online or at the Business Tax Office, listing the zoning clearance and, if you sell goods, the California seller's permit. Fees are due within 30 days of the business start date. Fee: Varies. https://oakland.hdlgov.com/

10. Registration Form for Commercial Employers, California Employment Development Department. Register in e-Services for Business within 15 days of paying over $100 in wages. Fee: Free. https://edd.ca.gov/en/payroll_taxes/save_time_and_register_online/

### Milk tea and bubble tea shops in Sacramento

1. Application for Employer Identification Number (EIN), Internal Revenue Service. Owners with an SSN or ITIN apply online. A company whose responsible party has neither (most China-based owners) faxes or mails Form SS-4, or calls the IRS international line. Fee: Free. https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/fss4.pdf
2. Articles of Organization (California LLC), California Secretary of State. Filed online in bizfile Online. Fee: $70. https://bizfileonline.sos.ca.gov/
3. Seller's permit, California Department of Tax and Fee Administration. Register online before your first sale; one permit for each location. Fee: Free. https://onlineservices.cdtfa.ca.gov/
4. Certified food protection manager, California Retail Food Code, enforced by the county or city environmental health department. An owner or employee of a place that prepares, handles or serves unpackaged perishable food passes a food protection manager exam from an accredited organization. A new place, a new owner, or a place that loses its certified person has 60 days to have one, and one person can't be certified for two locations. Keep the certificate on file for the inspector. Fee: Varies. http://publichealth.lacounty.gov/eh/business/certified-food-handler-manager.htm
5. City of Sacramento business tax certificate (Business Operations Tax), City of Sacramento Finance Department, Revenue Division. Every business operating in the City of Sacramento pays this yearly tax; the city issues no separate business license. Apply online, by email to finance@cityofsacramento.org, by mail or in person, and pay when you apply. The city sends the application to Community Development to confirm the zoning, then mails the certificate. Fee: Varies. https://cityofsacramento.gov/finance/revenue/business-operations-tax
6. Registration Form for Commercial Employers, California Employment Development Department. Register in e-Services for Business within 15 days of paying over $100 in wages. Fee: Free. https://edd.ca.gov/en/payroll_taxes/save_time_and_register_online/
7. Food facility plan review, Sacramento County Environmental Management Department. Needed to build a new food facility or convert a space into one. Mail or bring the application with one complete set of scaled plans and equipment spec sheets to 11080 White Rock Rd, Suite 200, Rancho Cordova, or email EHPlanReview@SacCounty.gov to submit electronically; three sets are needed at final approval. You're directed to the application to operate when you submit the plans. Fee: Varies. https://emd.saccounty.gov/content/dam/emd/docs/transition/Application%20for%20Food%20Facility%20Plan%20Review%202026-2027.pdf
8. Health permit to operate a food facility, Sacramento County Environmental Management Department. Submit the application to operate and pay the fees before the place opens. A certified food manager is needed within 60 days of opening, and every food employee needs a current food handler card. Fee: Varies. https://emd.saccounty.gov/EH/Documents/How%20to%20Obtain%20a%20Health%20Permit%2002-6-23.pdf
9. LLC annual tax ($800), California Franchise Tax Board. Paid every year by every LLC registered or doing business in California. Fee: $800. https://www.ftb.ca.gov/pay/

5. Customs Bond, U.S. Customs and Border Protection. Bought from a CBP-approved surety, usually through your customs broker, who files it electronically. A continuous bond covers a year of entries. Fee: Varies. https://www.cbp.gov/sites/default/files/2024-05/cbp_form_301.pdf

8. Product safety certificate, filed electronically at entry, U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission. The importer issues the certificate itself (there is no government form) and, under the eFiling rule, files the certificate data with CBP at entry. Fee: Free. https://www.cpsc.gov/eFiling
9. City of Sacramento business tax certificate (Business Operations Tax), City of Sacramento Finance Department, Revenue Division. Every business operating in the City of Sacramento pays this yearly tax; the city issues no separate business license. Apply online, by email to finance@cityofsacramento.org, by mail or in person, and pay when you apply. The city sends the application to Community Development to confirm the zoning, then mails the certificate. Fee: Varies. https://cityofsacramento.gov/finance/revenue/business-operations-tax

11. LLC annual tax ($800), California Franchise Tax Board. Paid every year by every LLC registered or doing business in California. Fee: $800. https://www.ftb.ca.gov/pay/
12. Packaging producer registration (EPR), CalRecycle, through Circular Action Alliance. The brand owner or importer of packaged goods sold in California registers and reports with the producer organization. Fee: Varies. https://circularactionalliance.org/california
13. Proposition 65 warning labels, California Office of Environmental Health Hazard Assessment. Nothing is filed. Businesses with 10 or more employees warn before exposing Californians to listed chemicals, including online at checkout. Fee: Free. https://www.p65warnings.ca.gov/business-resources/frequently-asked-questions-businesses

8. Registration Form for Commercial Employers, California Employment Development Department. Register in e-Services for Business within 15 days of paying over $100 in wages. Fee: Free. https://edd.ca.gov/en/payroll_taxes/save_time_and_register_online/
9. LLC annual tax ($800), California Franchise Tax Board. Paid every year by every LLC registered or doing business in California. Fee: $800. https://www.ftb.ca.gov/pay/
10. Packaging producer registration (EPR), CalRecycle, through Circular Action Alliance. The brand owner or importer of packaged goods sold in California registers and reports with the producer organization. Fee: Varies. https://circularactionalliance.org/california
11. Proposition 65 warning labels, California Office of Environmental Health Hazard Assessment. Nothing is filed. Businesses with 10 or more employees warn before exposing Californians to listed chemicals, including online at checkout. Fee: Free. https://www.p65warnings.ca.gov/business-resources/frequently-asked-questions-businesses

### Importers and online sellers in Sacramento
https://placetta.com/guides/sacramento/importer-ecommerce.html
1. Application for Employer Identification Number (EIN), Internal Revenue Service. Owners with an SSN or ITIN apply online. 2. Articles of Organization (California LLC), California Secretary of State. Filed online in bizfile Online. Fee: $70. https://bizfileonline.sos.ca.gov/
3. Seller's permit, California Department of Tax and Fee Administration. Register online before your first sale; one permit for each location. Fee: Free. https://onlineservices.cdtfa.ca.gov/
4. Create/Update Importer Identity Form, U.S. Customs and Border Protection. Sent to CBP (usually through your customs broker), or created in the ACE portal. Needed before your first entry as importer of record. Fee: Free. https://www.cbp.gov/sites/default/files/2026-06/cbp_form_5106.pdf
5. Customs Bond, U.S. Customs and Border Protection. Bought from a CBP-approved surety, usually through your customs broker, who files it electronically. A continuous bond covers a year of entries. Fee: Varies. https://www.cbp.gov/sites/default/files/2024-05/cbp_form_301.pdf
6. ACE Secure Data Portal account for importers, U.S. Customs and Border Protection. Applied for online in ACE. Lets you see your entries, duties and bond. Fee: Free. https://www.cbp.gov/trade/automated/getting-started/portal-applying
7. Product safety certificate, filed electronically at entry, U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission. The importer issues the certificate itself (there is no government form) and, under the eFiling rule, files the certificate data with CBP at entry. Fee: Free. https://www.cpsc.gov/eFiling
8. City of Sacramento business tax certificate (Business Operations Tax), City of Sacramento Finance Department, Revenue Division. Every business operating in the City of Sacramento pays this yearly tax; the city issues no separate business license. Apply online, by email to finance@cityofsacramento.org, by mail or in person, and pay when you apply. The city sends the application to Community Development to confirm the zoning, then mails the certificate. Fee: Varies. https://cityofsacramento.gov/finance/revenue/business-operations-tax

10. Packaging producer registration (EPR), CalRecycle, through Circular Action Alliance. The brand owner or importer of packaged goods sold in California registers and reports with the producer organization. Fee: Varies. https://circularactionalliance.org/california
11. Proposition 65 warning labels, California Office of Environmental Health Hazard Assessment. Nothing is filed. Businesses with 10 or more employees warn before exposing Californians to listed chemicals, including online at checkout. Fee: Free. https://www.p65warnings.ca.gov/business-resources/frequently-asked-questions-businesses

Register online in Portland Revenue Online with the tax ID, entity type, locations and owners, or mail, fax or bring the paper form. Fee: Varies. https://pro.portland.gov/?Link=Register

Every employer with paid employees in Oregon registers before the first paycheck, online in Revenue Online or the Oregon Business Registry, or on the paper Combined Employer's Registration sent to the Employment Department. One number covers withholding, unemployment tax, the Workers' Benefit Fund and transit taxes. Fee: Varies. https://revenueonline.dor.oregon.gov/tap/_/?Link=BIN
4. Restaurant plan review, Multnomah County Environmental Health. Needed before opening a new restaurant or remodeling one. Send the plan review application, the plans and the fee; construction can start once the approval letter arrives. Fee: Varies. https://multco.us/file/restaurant_plan_review_application/download
5. Multnomah County restaurant license, Multnomah County Environmental Health. Send the license application and fee (it can go with the plan review), then call for the pre-opening inspection once construction is done; you get the license and can open after it passes. Restaurant workers need food handler cards. Fee: Varies. https://multco.us/file/restaurant/bed_&_breakfast_license_application/download

6. Customs Bond, U.S. Customs and Border Protection. Bought from a CBP-approved surety, usually through your customs broker, who files it electronically. A continuous bond covers a year of entries. Fee: Varies. https://www.cbp.gov/sites/default/files/2024-05/cbp_form_301.pdf

8. Cosmetic product listing (MoCRA), U.S. Food and Drug Administration. Filed online in Cosmetics Direct by the brand (the responsible person on the label), one listing per product. Fee: Free. https://www.fda.gov/cosmetics/registration-listing-cosmetic-product-facilities-and-products
9. Product safety certificate, filed electronically at entry, U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission. The importer issues the certificate itself (there is no government form) and, under the eFiling rule, files the certificate data with CBP at entry. Fee: Free. https://www.cpsc.gov/eFiling
10. Unemployment tax account, Texas Workforce Commission. Register online once you pay wages in Texas. Fee: Free. https://www.twc.texas.gov/services/register-tax

2. Certificate of Formation (Texas LLC), Texas Secretary of State. Filed online in SOSDirect, or by mail or fax. Fee: $300. https://www.sos.state.tx.us/corp/forms/205_boc.pdf
3. Assumed Name Certificate (DBA), Texas Secretary of State. Filed when the store trades under a name other than the legal name. Fee: $25. https://www.sos.state.tx.us/corp/forms/503_boc.pdf
4. Texas Sales and Use Tax Permit Application, Texas Comptroller of Public Accounts. Apply online in eSystems before your first sale; one permit for each location. Fee: Free. https://comptroller.texas.gov/taxes/permit/
5. Create/Update Importer Identity Form, U.S. Customs and Border Protection. Sent to CBP (usually through your customs broker), or created in the ACE portal. Needed before your first entry as importer of record. Fee: Free. https://www.cbp.gov/sites/default/files/2026-06/cbp_form_5106.pdf
6. Customs Bond, U.S. Customs and Border Protection. Bought from a CBP-approved surety, usually through your customs broker, who files it electronically. A continuous bond covers a year of entries. Fee: Varies. https://www.cbp.gov/sites/default/files/2024-05/cbp_form_301.pdf
7. ACE Secure Data Portal account for importers, U.S. Customs and Border Protection. Applied for online in ACE. Lets you see your entries, duties and bond. Fee: Free. https://www.cbp.gov/trade/automated/getting-started/portal-applying
8. Product safety certificate, filed electronically at entry, U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission. The importer issues the certificate itself (there is no government form) and, under the eFiling rule, files the certificate data with CBP at entry. Fee: Free. https://www.cpsc.gov/eFiling
9. Franchise tax annual report, Texas Comptroller of Public Accounts. Filed every year by May 15, even when no tax is due. Fee: Free. https://comptroller.texas.gov/taxes/franchise/
