10. Certificate of Occupancy, City of Plano Building Inspections. Required to occupy any nonresidential space, and again when the business, its name or owner changes or a new tenant moves in. Submit the packet with the application fee; Building Inspections, Planning and, for a restaurant, Environmental Health review it and inspect. It must be approved before staff move in, stock arrives or the doors open, and it's posted on site. Fee: Varies. https://content.civicplus.com/api/assets/tx-plano/d2490980-662a-4f38-8def-66070c8691e5
11. Franchise tax annual report, Texas Comptroller of Public Accounts. Filed every year by May 15, even when no tax is due. Fee: Free. https://comptroller.texas.gov/taxes/franchise/

### Milk tea and bubble tea shops in Arlington
https://placetta.com/guides/arlington/milk-tea-shop.html
1. Application for Employer Identification Number (EIN), Internal Revenue Service. Owners with an SSN or ITIN apply online. A company whose responsible party has neither (most China-based owners) faxes or mails Form SS-4, or calls the IRS international line. Fee: Free. https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/fss4.pdf
2. Virginia business tax registration, Virginia Department of Taxation. Every new business registers online with Virginia Tax, or on paper Form R-1 if it can't: sales and use tax for dealers, and employer withholding with Virginia employees. Fee: Varies. https://account.tax.virginia.gov/online-services/?link=businessregistration
3. Certified food protection manager, Virginia Department of Health, with local health departments. Every Virginia food establishment, unless exempt, has at least one employee with authority over food preparation and service who holds a food protection manager certificate from a program accredited through the Conference for Food Protection. Arlington and Fairfax County check for it before opening. Fee: Varies. https://www.vdh.virginia.gov/environmental-health/food-safety-in-virginia/cfpm/
4. Arlington County business license, Arlington County Commissioner of Revenue, Business Tax Division. After the state requirements and the county permits, register the business in CAPP, the county's online system; a Business Tax Inspector then contacts you to finish the license. Fee: Varies. https://www.arlingtonva.us/Government/Programs/Taxes/Business-License-and-Taxes
5. Unemployment insurance employer registration, Virginia Employment Commission. A business with employees in Virginia must by law register with the VEC: online through iFile and iReg, or by mailing the FC-27. Fee: Varies. https://vec.virginia.gov/tax-filing-registration
6. Food service plan review, Arlington County Public Health Division, Environmental Health Program. For a new place or a major alteration. Send the application with the building plans, site plan, equipment schedule and the certified food protection manager certificate to ehealth@arlingtonva.us or 2110 Washington Blvd, Suite 350, and pay the fee online. A pre-opening inspection with the equipment in place and working follows. Fee: $40. https://www.arlingtonva.us/files/sharedassets/public/v/7/health/documents/eh-applications/food-service-plan-review-application_2025.06.20.pdf
7. Arlington County food establishment license, Arlington County Public Health Division, Environmental Health Program. Any place selling prepared or packaged food needs the county's food establishment license. Before opening, a certified food protection manager must be in place and present during all operating hours. Fee: Varies. https://arlingtonva.us/Government/Programs/Health/Environmental-Health/Food-Establishment-Plans-Construction

3. Create/Update Importer Identity Form, U.S. Customs and Border Protection. Sent to CBP (usually through your customs broker), or created in the ACE portal. Needed before your first entry as importer of record. Fee: Free. https://www.cbp.gov/sites/default/files/2026-06/cbp_form_5106.pdf
4. Customs Bond, U.S. Customs and Border Protection. Bought from a CBP-approved surety, usually through your customs broker, who files it electronically. A continuous bond covers a year of entries. Fee: Varies. https://www.cbp.gov/sites/default/files/2024-05/cbp_form_301.pdf
5. ACE Secure Data Portal account for importers, U.S. Customs and Border Protection. Applied for online in ACE. Lets you see your entries, duties and bond. Fee: Free. https://www.cbp.gov/trade/automated/getting-started/portal-applying
6. Product safety certificate, filed electronically at entry, U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission. The importer issues the certificate itself (there is no government form) and, under the eFiling rule, files the certificate data with CBP at entry. Fee: Free. https://www.cpsc.gov/eFiling
7. Arlington County business license, Arlington County Commissioner of Revenue, Business Tax Division. After the state requirements and the county permits, register the business in CAPP, the county's online system; a Business Tax Inspector then contacts you to finish the license. Fee: Varies. https://www.arlingtonva.us/Government/Programs/Taxes/Business-License-and-Taxes

### Milk tea and bubble tea shops in Fairfax County
https://placetta.com/guides/fairfax-county/milk-tea-shop.html
1. Application for Employer Identification Number (EIN), Internal Revenue Service. Owners with an SSN or ITIN apply online. Every new business registers online with Virginia Tax, or on paper Form R-1 if it can't: sales and use tax for dealers, and employer withholding with Virginia employees. Fee: Varies. https://account.tax.virginia.gov/online-services/?link=businessregistration
3. Certified food protection manager, Virginia Department of Health, with local health departments. Every Virginia food establishment, unless exempt, has at least one employee with authority over food preparation and service who holds a food protection manager certificate from a program accredited through the Conference for Food Protection. Arlington and Fairfax County check for it before opening. Fee: Varies. https://www.vdh.virginia.gov/environmental-health/food-safety-in-virginia/cfpm/
4. Fairfax County business license (BPOL), Fairfax County Department of Tax Administration. Every business with a physical location in the county files within 75 days of starting there, or pays a 10% late penalty; no tax is owed until gross receipts pass $10,000 in a year. Inside the cities of Fairfax and Falls Church and the towns of Clifton, Herndon and Vienna, the license comes from that city or town instead. Fee: Varies. https://Www.Fairfaxcounty.Gov/taxes/sites/taxes/files/Assets/Documents/PDF/business/2024-BPOL-application-instruction-fillable.pdf
5. Unemployment insurance employer registration, Virginia Employment Commission. A business with employees in Virginia must by law register with the VEC: online through iFile and iReg, or by mailing the FC-27. Fee: Varies. https://vec.virginia.gov/tax-filing-registration
6. Food establishment plan review, Fairfax County Health Department, Division of Environmental Health. Plans go in through the PLUS portal before construction, remodeling or conversion starts; work can't begin until the Health Department finishes its commercial plan review. Fee: Varies. https://plus.fairfaxcounty.gov
7. Non-Residential Use Permit, Fairfax County Land Development Services. Under the zoning ordinance no commercial space may be occupied, and no use changed, until this permit is approved; it is the county's certificate of use and occupancy. Applied for in PLUS. After opening, book the Fire Marshal's post-occupancy inspection within 10 days. Fee: Varies. https://plus.fairfaxcounty.gov/CitizenAccess/Welcome.aspx
8. Food establishment permit to operate, Fairfax County Health Department, Division of Environmental Health. Apply in PLUS, then call at least 3 days ahead for the pre-occupancy inspection, where a food manager with an accredited exam certificate must be present. The permit to operate is issued once the inspection passes. Fee: Varies. https://plus.fairfaxcounty.gov

3. Create/Update Importer Identity Form, U.S. Customs and Border Protection. Sent to CBP (usually through your customs broker), or created in the ACE portal. Needed before your first entry as importer of record. Fee: Free. https://www.cbp.gov/sites/default/files/2026-06/cbp_form_5106.pdf
4. Customs Bond, U.S. Customs and Border Protection. Bought from a CBP-approved surety, usually through your customs broker, who files it electronically. A continuous bond covers a year of entries. Fee: Varies. https://www.cbp.gov/sites/default/files/2024-05/cbp_form_301.pdf
5. Product safety certificate, filed electronically at entry, U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission. The importer issues the certificate itself (there is no government form) and, under the eFiling rule, files the certificate data with CBP at entry. Fee: Free. https://www.cpsc.gov/eFiling
6. Fairfax County business license (BPOL), Fairfax County Department of Tax Administration. Every business with a physical location in the county files within 75 days of starting there, or pays a 10% late penalty; no tax is owed until gross receipts pass $10,000 in a year. Inside the cities of Fairfax and Falls Church and the towns of Clifton, Herndon and Vienna, the license comes from that city or town instead. Fee: Varies. https://Www.Fairfaxcounty.Gov/taxes/sites/taxes/files/Assets/Documents/PDF/business/2024-BPOL-application-instruction-fillable.pdf
7. Unemployment insurance employer registration, Virginia Employment Commission. A business with employees in Virginia must by law register with the VEC: online through iFile and iReg, or by mailing the FC-27. Fee: Varies. https://vec.virginia.gov/tax-filing-registration
8. Non-Residential Use Permit, Fairfax County Land Development Services. Under the zoning ordinance no commercial space may be occupied, and no use changed, until this permit is approved; it is the county's certificate of use and occupancy. Applied for in PLUS. After opening, book the Fire Marshal's post-occupancy inspection within 10 days. Fee: Varies. https://plus.fairfaxcounty.gov/CitizenAccess/Welcome.aspx

Everyone doing business in New Jersey registers; NJ-REG is the tax and employer registration, filed online at least 15 business days before opening. 4. Food establishment plan review, Edison Township Department of Health. Edison's Division of Health reviews plans for food establishments, for a fee the township code sets. 5. Edison retail food license, Edison Township Department of Health. Restaurants and food stores apply to the township with Division of Health approval, at 100 Municipal Boulevard. Every food handler and supervisor completes a food handling course the Division of Health accepts within a year of starting work. Fee: Varies. https://cms2.revize.com/revize/edisonnj/document_center/Retail%20Food%20Fillable%20Application.pdf

### Milk tea and bubble tea shops in Denver
https://placetta.com/guides/denver/milk-tea-shop.html
1. Application for Employer Identification Number (EIN), Internal Revenue Service. Owners with an SSN or ITIN apply online. A company whose responsible party has neither (most China-based owners) faxes or mails Form SS-4, or calls the IRS international line. Fee: Free. https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/fss4.pdf
2. Colorado sales tax and withholding registration, Colorado Department of Revenue. A business with a Colorado location applies in MyBizColorado for the sales tax license and the wage withholding account (or on paper Form CR0100); MyBizColorado also connects you with the Department of Labor and Employment to set up unemployment insurance. Fee: Varies. https://mybiz.colorado.gov/
3. Denver sales tax license, City and County of Denver, Department of Finance, Treasury. Denver collects its own sales tax: a Denver business making retail sales registers in the eBiz Tax Center. With staff working in Denver, also register for the Occupational Privilege Tax. Fee: Free. https://www.denvergov.org/ebiztax
4. Denver zoning use permit, Denver Community Planning and Development. Apply on e-permits (select Zoning Permit); the permit is issued once its fee is paid, and lapses unless a building permit or certificate of occupancy follows within 180 days. Denver's retail food license won't issue without it. Fee: Varies. https://denvergov.org/Government/Agencies-Departments-Offices/Agencies-Departments-Offices-Directory/Community-Planning-and-Development/Plan-Review-Permits-and-Inspections/Zoning-Permits/Apply-for-Commercial-Zoning-Permits
5. Food establishment plan review, Denver Department of Public Health and Environment. Denver Public Health lists plan review among the steps to open a food business, and its inspection comes before the retail food license. Fee: Varies. https://denvergov.org/Government/Agencies-Departments-Offices/Agencies-Departments-Offices-Directory/Public-Health-Environment/Public-Health-Investigations/Plan-Review-and-Inspections
6. Denver retail food establishment license, City and County of Denver, Business Licensing. Apply in Denver's Online Permitting and Licensing Center with the entity and on-site manager details, and the Denver sales tax license if you sell taxable goods. After review, Development Services, the Fire Department, Public Health and Zoning inspect. Fee: Varies. https://www.denvergov.org/Government/Agencies-Departments-Offices/Agencies-Departments-Offices-Directory/Business-Licensing/Business-licenses/Retail-Food/Retail-food/New

### Cosmetics stores in Denver
https://placetta.com/guides/denver/cosmetics-store.html
1. Application for Employer Identification Number (EIN), Internal Revenue Service. Owners with an SSN or ITIN apply online. A company whose responsible party has neither (most China-based owners) faxes or mails Form SS-4, or calls the IRS international line. Fee: Free. https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/fss4.pdf

Fee: Varies. https://mybiz.colorado.gov/
3. Create/Update Importer Identity Form, U.S. Customs and Border Protection. Sent to CBP (usually through your customs broker), or created in the ACE portal. Needed before your first entry as importer of record. Fee: Free. https://www.cbp.gov/sites/default/files/2026-06/cbp_form_5106.pdf
4. Customs Bond, U.S. Customs and Border Protection. Bought from a CBP-approved surety, usually through your customs broker, who files it electronically. A continuous bond covers a year of entries. Fee: Varies. https://www.cbp.gov/sites/default/files/2024-05/cbp_form_301.pdf
5. Cosmetic product facility registration (MoCRA), U.S. Food and Drug Administration. Filed online in Cosmetics Direct by the facility that makes or processes the cosmetics. Fee: Free. https://www.fda.gov/cosmetics/registration-listing-cosmetic-product-facilities-and-products
6. Cosmetic product listing (MoCRA), U.S. Food and Drug Administration. Filed online in Cosmetics Direct by the brand (the responsible person on the label), one listing per product. Fee: Free. https://www.fda.gov/cosmetics/registration-listing-cosmetic-product-facilities-and-products
7. Product safety certificate, filed electronically at entry, U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission. The importer issues the certificate itself (there is no government form) and, under the eFiling rule, files the certificate data with CBP at entry. Fee: Free. https://www.cpsc.gov/eFiling
8. Denver sales tax license, City and County of Denver, Department of Finance, Treasury. Denver collects its own sales tax: a Denver business making retail sales registers in the eBiz Tax Center. With staff working in Denver, also register for the Occupational Privilege Tax. Fee: Free. https://www.denvergov.org/ebiztax

### Milk tea and bubble tea shops in Minneapolis
https://placetta.com/guides/minneapolis/milk-tea-shop.html
1. Application for Employer Identification Number (EIN), Internal Revenue Service. Owners with an SSN or ITIN apply online. A company whose responsible party has neither (most China-based owners) faxes or mails Form SS-4, or calls the IRS international line. Fee: Free. https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/fss4.pdf
2. Minnesota tax ID and sales tax registration, Minnesota Department of Revenue. Before any taxable sale, get a Minnesota Tax ID and a sales and use tax account in e-Services, or by phone at 651-282-5225. Fee: Varies. https://www.mndor.state.mn.us/tp/eservices/_/?link=NewBusinessReg
3. Minnesota certified food protection manager, Minnesota Department of Health. Food establishments, unless exempt, employ a Minnesota CFPM and display the certificate. Pass an approved course and exam, then apply online within six months of the exam. A newly opening place may start with someone who passed within the last six months, who then has 60 days to get certified. Fee: Varies. https://mn-mdh.portal.opengov.com/categories/1087/record-types/6498
4. Unemployment insurance employer registration, Minnesota Unemployment Insurance Program (DEED). Every employer paying covered wages in Minnesota registers in Employer Self-Service, online or by phone, as soon as possible after the first wages and before the first quarterly wage detail report is due. Fee: Varies. https://www1.ui.mn.gov/ui_employer/ui/employer/login
5. Food plan review, City of Minneapolis, Development Review. The city approves the plans before any work on a new food business, a remodel or expansion, equipment that needs gas, mechanical or plumbing permits, or ventless cooking. Email the application to Development@minneapolismn.gov, upload the documents through the ProjectDox link you get back, and a plan reviewer visits the site. Fee: Varies. https://www.minneapolismn.gov/media/-www-content-assets/documents/Food-Plan-Review-Application-(July-2026).pdf
6. Minneapolis restaurant license, City of Minneapolis, Business Licenses, with Environmental Health. Needed for food or drinks made for dining in, carryout or delivery: a restaurant license with 13 or more seats, a food manufacturer license with 12 or fewer (one application covers both). Apply at least four weeks before opening, after the plans are approved. Fee: Varies. https://www.minneapolismn.gov/business-services/licenses-permits-inspections/business-licenses/food-restaurants/restaurant-coffee-cafe/restaurant/application/

Pass an approved course and exam, then apply online within six months of the exam. A newly opening place may start with someone who passed within the last six months, who then has 60 days to get certified. Fee: Varies. https://mn-mdh.portal.opengov.com/categories/1087/record-types/6498
4. Unemployment insurance employer registration, Minnesota Unemployment Insurance Program (DEED). Every employer paying covered wages in Minnesota registers in Employer Self-Service, online or by phone, as soon as possible after the first wages and before the first quarterly wage detail report is due. Fee: Varies. https://www1.ui.mn.gov/ui_employer/ui/employer/login
5. Food plan review, City of Minneapolis, Development Review. The city approves the plans before any work on a new food business, a remodel or expansion, equipment that needs gas, mechanical or plumbing permits, or ventless cooking. Email the application to Development@minneapolismn.gov, upload the documents through the ProjectDox link you get back, and a plan reviewer visits the site. Fee: Varies. https://www.minneapolismn.gov/media/-www-content-assets/documents/Food-Plan-Review-Application-(July-2026).pdf
6. Minneapolis restaurant license, City of Minneapolis, Business Licenses, with Environmental Health. Needed for food or drinks made for dining in, carryout or delivery: a restaurant license with 13 or more seats, a food manufacturer license with 12 or fewer (one application covers both). Apply at least four weeks before opening, after the plans are approved. Fee: Varies. https://www.minneapolismn.gov/business-services/licenses-permits-inspections/business-licenses/food-restaurants/restaurant-coffee-cafe/restaurant/application/

### Cosmetics stores in Minneapolis
https://placetta.com/guides/minneapolis/cosmetics-store.html
1. Application for Employer Identification Number (EIN), Internal Revenue Service. Owners with an SSN or ITIN apply online. 3. Create/Update Importer Identity Form, U.S. Customs and Border Protection. Sent to CBP (usually through your customs broker), or created in the ACE portal. Needed before your first entry as importer of record. Fee: Free. https://www.cbp.gov/sites/default/files/2026-06/cbp_form_5106.pdf
4. Customs Bond, U.S. Customs and Border Protection. Bought from a CBP-approved surety, usually through your customs broker, who files it electronically. A continuous bond covers a year of entries. Fee: Varies. https://www.cbp.gov/sites/default/files/2024-05/cbp_form_301.pdf
5. Cosmetic product facility registration (MoCRA), U.S. Food and Drug Administration. Filed online in Cosmetics Direct by the facility that makes or processes the cosmetics. Fee: Free. https://www.fda.gov/cosmetics/registration-listing-cosmetic-product-facilities-and-products
6. Cosmetic product listing (MoCRA), U.S. Food and Drug Administration. Filed online in Cosmetics Direct by the brand (the responsible person on the label), one listing per product. Fee: Free. https://www.fda.gov/cosmetics/registration-listing-cosmetic-product-facilities-and-products
7. Product safety certificate, filed electronically at entry, U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission. The importer issues the certificate itself (there is no government form) and, under the eFiling rule, files the certificate data with CBP at entry. Fee: Free. https://www.cpsc.gov/eFiling
8. Unemployment insurance employer registration, Minnesota Unemployment Insurance Program (DEED). Every employer paying covered wages in Minnesota registers in Employer Self-Service, online or by phone, as soon as possible after the first wages and before the first quarterly wage detail report is due. ### Milk tea and bubble tea shops in Columbus
https://placetta.com/guides/columbus/milk-tea-shop.html
1. Application for Employer Identification Number (EIN), Internal Revenue Service. Owners with an SSN or ITIN apply online. A company whose responsible party has neither (most China-based owners) faxes or mails Form SS-4, or calls the IRS international line. Fee: Free. https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/fss4.pdf
2. Ohio vendor's license (sales tax), Franklin County Auditor, for the Ohio Department of Taxation. A business with a location in Franklin County gets its sales tax account from the County Auditor: complete the ST 1 online, or mail it with the fee to 373 S High St, 21st floor, Columbus. Check with the local zoning department about the address first. Fee: $50. https://franklincountyohio.jotform.com/form/222723544220143
3. Food safety certification for the person in charge, Ohio Department of Health, with the local health district. Ohio's rule asks a food service operation of risk level I to IV, first licensed after March 1, 2010, for at least one person in charge on every shift with person in charge certification; someone with manager certification in food protection doesn't need it. Columbus Public Health teaches a 4-hour person in charge course and the 16-hour ServSafe course. Fee: Varies. https://odh.ohio.gov/know-our-programs/food-safety-program/food-safety-certification/
4. Unemployment insurance employer account, Ohio Department of Job and Family Services, Office of Unemployment Insurance Operations. A new employer creates an OHIO UI account and registers it in the Ohio Unemployment SOURCE employer portal. Fee: Varies. https://thesource.jfs.ohio.gov/employer.html
5. Food service plan review, Columbus Public Health, Food Protection Program. Needed for a new site, a major remodel, or a change of business type or owner, before licensing. Send the plan review packet with payment to EH@Columbus.gov. Covers the cities of Columbus and Worthington. Fee: Varies. https://www.columbus.gov/files/sharedassets/city/v/10/public-health/planreview-application.pdf
6. Columbus food service license, Columbus Public Health, Food Protection Program. Once the plans are approved and the work is done, complete the license application and ask for the final inspection at least three business days before opening; a new building needs Building Services' final approval first. The license fee is collected at the inspection and the printed license is mailed. Fee: Varies. https://www.columbus.gov/Services/Food-Protection-Program

### Dessert shops in Columbus
https://placetta.com/guides/columbus/dessert-shop.html
1. Application for Employer Identification Number (EIN), Internal Revenue Service. Owners with an SSN or ITIN apply online. A company whose responsible party has neither (most China-based owners) faxes or mails Form SS-4, or calls the IRS international line. Fee: Free. https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/fss4.pdf
2. Ohio vendor's license (sales tax), Franklin County Auditor, for the Ohio Department of Taxation. A business with a location in Franklin County gets its sales tax account from the County Auditor: complete the ST 1 online, or mail it with the fee to 373 S High St, 21st floor, Columbus. Check with the local zoning department about the address first. Fee: $50. https://franklincountyohio.jotform.com/form/222723544220143
3. Food safety certification for the person in charge, Ohio Department of Health, with the local health district. Ohio's rule asks a food service operation of risk level I to IV, first licensed after March 1, 2010, for at least one person in charge on every shift with person in charge certification; someone with manager certification in food protection doesn't need it. Columbus Public Health teaches a 4-hour person in charge course and the 16-hour ServSafe course. Fee: Varies. https://odh.ohio.gov/know-our-programs/food-safety-program/food-safety-certification/
4. Unemployment insurance employer account, Ohio Department of Job and Family Services, Office of Unemployment Insurance Operations. A new employer creates an OHIO UI account and registers it in the Ohio Unemployment SOURCE employer portal. Fee: Varies. https://thesource.jfs.ohio.gov/employer.html
5. Food service plan review, Columbus Public Health, Food Protection Program. Needed for a new site, a major remodel, or a change of business type or owner, before licensing. Send the plan review packet with payment to EH@Columbus.gov. Covers the cities of Columbus and Worthington. Fee: Varies. https://www.columbus.gov/files/sharedassets/city/v/10/public-health/planreview-application.pdf
6. Columbus food service license, Columbus Public Health, Food Protection Program. Once the plans are approved and the work is done, complete the license application and ask for the final inspection at least three business days before opening; a new building needs Building Services' final approval first. The license fee is collected at the inspection and the printed license is mailed. Fee: Varies. https://www.columbus.gov/Services/Food-Protection-Program

### Cosmetics stores in Columbus
https://placetta.com/guides/columbus/cosmetics-store.html
1. Application for Employer Identification Number (EIN), Internal Revenue Service. Owners with an SSN or ITIN apply online. A company whose responsible party has neither (most China-based owners) faxes or mails Form SS-4, or calls the IRS international line. Fee: Free. https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/fss4.pdf
2. Ohio vendor's license (sales tax), Franklin County Auditor, for the Ohio Department of Taxation. A business with a location in Franklin County gets its sales tax account from the County Auditor: complete the ST 1 online, or mail it with the fee to 373 S High St, 21st floor, Columbus. Check with the local zoning department about the address first. Fee: $50. https://franklincountyohio.jotform.com/form/222723544220143
3. Create/Update Importer Identity Form, U.S. Customs and Border Protection. Sent to CBP (usually through your customs broker), or created in the ACE portal. Needed before your first entry as importer of record. Fee: Free. https://www.cbp.gov/sites/default/files/2026-06/cbp_form_5106.pdf
4. Customs Bond, U.S. Customs and Border Protection. Bought from a CBP-approved surety, usually through your customs broker, who files it electronically. A continuous bond covers a year of entries. Fee: Varies. https://www.cbp.gov/sites/default/files/2024-05/cbp_form_301.pdf
5. Cosmetic product facility registration (MoCRA), U.S. Food and Drug Administration. Filed online in Cosmetics Direct by the facility that makes or processes the cosmetics. Fee: Free. https://www.fda.gov/cosmetics/registration-listing-cosmetic-product-facilities-and-products
6. Cosmetic product listing (MoCRA), U.S. Food and Drug Administration. Filed online in Cosmetics Direct by the brand (the responsible person on the label), one listing per product. Fee: Free. https://www.fda.gov/cosmetics/registration-listing-cosmetic-product-facilities-and-products
7. Product safety certificate, filed electronically at entry, U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission. The importer issues the certificate itself (there is no government form) and, under the eFiling rule, files the certificate data with CBP at entry. Fee: Free. https://www.cpsc.gov/eFiling
8. Unemployment insurance employer account, Ohio Department of Job and Family Services, Office of Unemployment Insurance Operations. A new employer creates an OHIO UI account and registers it in the Ohio Unemployment SOURCE employer portal. Fee: Varies. https://thesource.jfs.ohio.gov/employer.html

### Importers and online sellers in Columbus
https://placetta.com/guides/columbus/importer-ecommerce.html
1. Application for Employer Identification Number (EIN), Internal Revenue Service. Owners with an SSN or ITIN apply online. A company whose responsible party has neither (most China-based owners) faxes or mails Form SS-4, or calls the IRS international line. Fee: Free. https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/fss4.pdf
2. Ohio vendor's license (sales tax), Franklin County Auditor, for the Ohio Department of Taxation. A business with a location in Franklin County gets its sales tax account from the County Auditor: complete the ST 1 online, or mail it with the fee to 373 S High St, 21st floor, Columbus. 5. ACE Secure Data Portal account for importers, U.S. Customs and Border Protection. Applied for online in ACE. Lets you see your entries, duties and bond. Fee: Free. https://www.cbp.gov/trade/automated/getting-started/portal-applying
6. Product safety certificate, filed electronically at entry, U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission. The importer issues the certificate itself (there is no government form) and, under the eFiling rule, files the certificate data with CBP at entry. Fee: Free. https://www.cpsc.gov/eFiling

### Warehouses and 3PLs in Columbus
https://placetta.com/guides/columbus/warehouse-3pl.html
1. Application for Employer Identification Number (EIN), Internal Revenue Service. Owners with an SSN or ITIN apply online. A company whose responsible party has neither (most China-based owners) faxes or mails Form SS-4, or calls the IRS international line. Fee: Free. https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/fss4.pdf
2. Create/Update Importer Identity Form, U.S. Customs and Border Protection. Sent to CBP (usually through your customs broker), or created in the ACE portal. Needed before your first entry as importer of record. Fee: Free. https://www.cbp.gov/sites/default/files/2026-06/cbp_form_5106.pdf
3. Customs Bond, U.S. Customs and Border Protection. Bought from a CBP-approved surety, usually through your customs broker, who files it electronically. A continuous bond covers a year of entries. Fee: Varies. https://www.cbp.gov/sites/default/files/2024-05/cbp_form_301.pdf
4. ACE Secure Data Portal account for importers, U.S. Customs and Border Protection. Applied for online in ACE. Lets you see your entries, duties and bond. Fee: Free. https://www.cbp.gov/trade/automated/getting-started/portal-applying
5. Hazardous materials registration, Pipeline and Hazardous Materials Safety Administration (DOT). Filed online when you ship or offer certain hazardous materials in bulk, such as large lithium battery shipments. Fee: Varies. https://hazmatonline.phmsa.dot.gov/services/
6. Unemployment insurance employer account, Ohio Department of Job and Family Services, Office of Unemployment Insurance Operations. A new employer creates an OHIO UI account and registers it in the Ohio Unemployment SOURCE employer portal. Fee: Varies. https://thesource.jfs.ohio.gov/employer.html
